title: Psychologist, psychotherapist or coach: the differences in Italy – Blooming
description: What psychologists, psychotherapists, psychiatrists, coaches and counsellors do in Italy, who does what at Blooming, and how to choose. Not sure? Start with a free 30-minute first meeting.

data.title: Psychologist, psychotherapist or coach: the differences, and who does what at Blooming.

p.t: Professional titles don't always mean the same thing from one country to another, so what you called a therapist or a counsellor at home may correspond to a different title here. This page explains what each title means in Italy, who does what at Blooming, and how to choose.

data.title: Five titles you may come across, and what they mean in Italy.

p.t: A psychologist has a degree in psychology and is registered with the Order of Psychologists of their region, which keeps a public register you can check. On this site we call it the Italian Order of Psychologists. Psychologists can offer psychological assessment and support, and many also work in career guidance.

items.note: Scope: to verify with a source, e.g. Law 56/1989.

p.t: A psychotherapist is a psychologist or a medical doctor who has completed at least four years of specialist training in psychotherapy. Psychotherapy is for difficulties that go deeper or have lasted a long time.

items.note: Four years: to verify with a source. Usually longer than psychological support: to confirm with Monica.

p.t: A psychiatrist is a medical doctor who specialises in mental health and can prescribe medication. Blooming doesn't offer psychiatry.
Coaching isn't a regulated profession in Italy, so coaches come from many different backgrounds and kinds of training. Coaching works on goals and next steps, usually at work, and it isn't therapy.

items.note: Not regulated: to check with your own adviser.

p.t: In the UK and many other countries, "counselling" is a common word for talking therapy. In Italy the word is used differently. If you're looking for what you'd have called counselling at home, the closest service at Blooming is psychological support.

items.note: Wording to check with your own adviser.

data.title: Career work and therapy, each with its own psychologist.

p.t: Career coaching & guidance and workplace coaching
are with a psychologist, registered since 2014, who has worked in HR for over ten years. She works in English. She isn't a psychotherapist.
Psychological support and psychotherapy
are with a psychologist, registered since 2010, who is a cognitive behavioural psychotherapist.

So the person coaching you is a psychologist who has spent years in HR and knows the Italian job market. And because trouble at work and a hard time at home often make each other worse, the coach and the therapist can bring each other in, with your consent.

blocks.note: Only if Monica confirms English: ", in English and Italian". If not: ". Her sessions are in Italian." · How information is shared, and its limits: to define with the practice; check with your own adviser.

data.title: Start from what's going on, not from the job title.

p.t: You and your new manager keep clashing, and every meeting leaves you tense.
Workplace coaching.
You're weighing up whether to take a job in another city, retrain or stay where you are.
Career coaching & guidance.
Your mother, in another country, has just been diagnosed with a serious illness, and you can't concentrate on anything else.
Psychological support.
Panic has been building for months, and you've started avoiding the places where it happens.
Psychotherapy.
You think you may need medication.
A psychiatrist, or your GP to start with. Blooming doesn't offer psychiatry.
It's normal for the line not to be clear. When it isn't, the free first meeting is there to sort it out.

data.title: You don't need to choose before you book.

p.t: In a free 30-minute video call, you describe what's going on and find out which kind of help fits, and with whom. It isn't a session or an assessment.

When you book, you choose the kind of help, or "Not sure yet", and the language. The psychologist you meet works out with you what fits. If it turns out to be another psychologist's area, she can suggest her colleague.
